tool.name: search_stories
tool.title: GDELT Cloud: search stories
tool.description: Retrieve a bounded reporting sample. For counts or period comparisons, call summarize_stories first with identical structured filters. Use summarize_events for Event metrics, then sample relevant Stories for evidence. A Story mention or passenger-service disruption does not prove freight impact. Continuous stories coverage begins 2026-03-08. Use consecutive windows of at most 30 inclusive days; a calendar month can be too long. Finish pagination.next_cursor within each fixed window before starting the next chunk without a cursor. Without an explicit window, entity filters default to 30 days and other queries to the last 24 hours. meta.query_window reports the effective predicates; meta.coverage describes the available corpus. Search v2 clustered Stories when the user needs narrative clusters and article evidence. Supports plain-English geography whose region/continent filters expand to country lists and match through linked Event location, optional admin1, linked Event category/subcategory filters, linked-event/fatality filters, article_count_min/article_count_max, true embedding semantic search, and significance or recent sorting. Returns Story cards with public GDELT Cloud URLs, linked Events/Entities, top 3 articles inline, source favicons, article sharing images, and linked Entity thumbnails when available. Entity matching uses coverage: the entity appears in the Story, which does not establish that it is a party to its events. For ongoing collectors and company watches, discover get_activity (recorded time) and read_resource skill://building-with-api/SKILL.md before coding checkpoints; reporting-date searches are not an arrival feed. Country matching defaults to location_or_actor_origin; for territorial scope use country_match=location and check the echo on both news surfaces.

bbox.description: Geographic bounding box 'lat_min,lon_min,lat_max,lon_max'. Monitor place/facility replay requests supply this exact filter.

days.description: Window days. Omit for the REST default: 30 days with entity, rolling past 24 hours otherwise. Set only to deliberately change that window.

sort.description: 'significance' ranks by canonical product importance; 'recent' ranks newest first.

limit.description: Number of Story cards to return. Each card includes top 3 inline articles only.

admin1.description: Optional state/province/admin1 name discovered with list_admin1. Filters Story/Event location only, not actor origin. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'admin1').

cursor.description: Continuation from pagination.next_cursor in the previous response. Keep the other filters unchanged; null means no next page.

domain.description: Deprecated legacy linked CAMEO+ domain filter. Prefer category='DEMOGRAPHIC' and other category values for new integrations.

entity.description: Resolved terminal entity id, news id, or name. Uses the same shared resolver as Events and entity products. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'entity').

office.description: Political office ID (Q… or p_…), resolved with offices_search. Matches published term holders overlapping the reporting window or office_as_of. Unioned with entity=; refuses >1,000 holders. applied_filters.office_holders reports unresolved news identities. Actor context, not screening. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'office').

region.description: One plain-English region (Middle East, Europe, South Asia, Western Africa, …). Expanded to its ISO-3 country list and applied the same way as `country`.

search.description: Search text. With search_mode=lexical this is a literal phrase in served Events title/summary or Stories title. By default the complete phrase is checked against name/title evidence and is also embedded for vector ranking; literal matches rank first and remaining results are conceptual neighbours. There is no boolean parser: a query shaped `a OR b` is reduced to its first term and the response says so. Costs an embedding call and can return 503 SEMANTIC_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE.

country.description: One or more plain-English country names or ISO-3 codes; legacy FIPS aliases also accepted. Filters Stories through linked-Event location. For a single country pass a one-element list: country=['United States']. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'country').

related.description: Attach a `related` block to each Story: the distinct Stories belonging to the same ongoing situation, with a count and their combined article total. A border crossing and the government's response to it are two Stories in one situation — both stay separately retrievable. Set false to skip the lookup.

category.description: One category string from linked Event taxonomy. Use categories for multiple choices. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'category').

end_date.description: Inclusive end date in YYYY-MM-DD. With days only, start_date is computed as the trailing window ending here. Defaults to today UTC.

continent.description: One plain-English continent (Asia, Europe, Africa, North America, South America, Oceania). Expanded to its ISO-3 country list and applied the same way as `country`.

languages.description: ISO source-language filter, e.g. ['ar','zh','en']. Restricts Stories to those with source-article coverage in these languages, for comparing narrative coverage across language spheres. Omit for all languages. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'languages').

categories.description: JSON array (OR combined), e.g. ["INFRASTRUCTURE", "ECONOMIC"], not a JSON-encoded string. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'categories').

has_events.description: Default unset returns BOTH narrative Stories and event-coded Stories — prefer this for broader coverage. Stories represent narrative clusters; not every cluster has yet been coded as a structured Event, so requiring events silently drops the majority of relevant stories. Only set true when the analysis specifically needs structured-event metrics (significance, goldstein, fatalities, etc.). Set false to isolate narrative-only clusters — useful for comparing narrative coverage to coded events on the same topic.

start_date.description: Inclusive start date in YYYY-MM-DD. With end_date, defines an explicit MCP Story window of at most 30 days.

target_ids.description: Comma-separated stable IDs for the selected roots (up to 25). Use with target_type; roots are unioned. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'target_ids').

search_mode.description: Search interpretation. semantic is a bounded hybrid search: complete-phrase name/title matches rank ahead of vector-ranked conceptual neighbours. lexical filters the complete serving set for a case-insensitive literal phrase in Events title/summary or Stories title before pagination; no stemming or boolean parsing. Lexical mode requires a supported serving snapshot and never falls back to the warehouse.

subcategory.description: Linked-Event subcategory string validated at runtime and scoped by category/categories. Conflict values are labels such as Peaceful protest; CAMEO+ values should be stable codes such as TE01 or IN03, with codebook labels accepted as legacy aliases. Choices: get_parameter_options('search_stories', 'subcategory').

target_type.description: Typed selected root for a shared connected scope: entity or facility. Use with target_ids.

entity_match.description: Entity matching uses coverage through a linked Story. The entity appears in that Story; this does not establish that it is an actor or party to the Event. Omit to inherit the API default, or explicitly select coverage.

office_as_of.description: Valid-time date for office= (YYYY-MM-DD): who held it on this publisher-stated date. Separate from reporting dates and knowledge-time replay. Missing term evidence is excluded, never guessed.

recorded_end.description: Exclusive end of API publication time, as an ISO UTC timestamp. Supply both bounds. Includes late arrivals without changing when the event happened. Cannot combine with reporting-date filters. Event and Story lists return records first made available in this interval, not later updates to existing records. Use /api/v2/activity for changes.

country_match.description: Which definition of "in this country" the `country` / `region` / `continent` filters use. Applies to `region` and `continent` too, since both expand into the same country set. Note that `group_by=country` buckets on the event's own location, while the default match also admits actor origin — so a filtered total and the bucket for that same country can differ. Pass `country_match=location` when you need the two to agree.

entity_family.description: Which canonical ids the handle stands for. `expand` (default) also matches the sibling ids the entity arbiter has already merged into the same real-world entity — a Wikipedia identity minted twice under different URL spellings, for instance — and echoes the union back as `applied_filters.entity_ids_expanded`. `exact` restricts to the one canonical id the handle resolves to, reproducing the pre-2026-08-25 counts.

related_scope.description: direct matches the selected target. connected includes verified controlled subsidiaries for entities, or identified facility owners and authoritative parent paths for facilities.

response_mode.description: Compact chat projection or unchanged bounded full API response; neither fetches another page.

event_category.description: Deprecated alias for category. Prefer category='Battles' or category='CRIME'.

tool.name: summarize_events
tool.title: GDELT Cloud: summarize events
tool.description: For occurrences inside a country, explicitly set country_match=location on both periods; the default also includes actor origins abroad. Compare identical filters and all four core metrics. A broad Infrastructure category count is not transport disruption: select the relevant taxonomy subcategory and group_by=subcategory before making that claim. Then search_events for evidence. Continuous events coverage begins 2026-03-01. Use consecutive windows of at most 30 inclusive days; a calendar month can be too long. This summary endpoint does not support cursor pagination; request each date chunk separately. Without an explicit window, entity filters default to 30 days and other queries to the last 24 hours. meta.query_window reports the effective predicates; meta.coverage describes the available corpus. Quantify GDELT Cloud Event counts and aggregates by date, geography or taxonomy before sampling evidence. Use group_by='subcategory' under a parent category such as Battles to discover ACLED sub-event buckets like Government regains territory, then reuse category+subcategory in search_events. Accepts the same structured and metric filters as search_events except semantic search. Returns counts plus grouped aggregate statistics. Favor the four core metrics: CAMEO+ magnitude, systemic importance, propagation potential and market sensitivity; significance is a ranking aid, not a disruption-pressure index. Use returned non-null metric counts and coverage; do not average displayed samples or unrelated categories. Hide coding confidence in ordinary answers. Additional evidence includes fatalities and article counts. For country/region briefs read_resource skill://news-country-research/SKILL.md. Compare the requested subtype, not all parent-category Events; discover subcategory buckets first and keep identical filters across windows. Use for comparable filtered populations, not totals inferred from sampled pages; counts describe reporting, not independently verified damage.

days.description: Calendar-date window ending today, in days (max 30). `window=7d` and `days=7` are equivalent. When omitted, a request without entity filters uses the last 24 hours; entity filters use 30 days. Read meta.query_window for the actual bounds. There is no equivalent numeric default: sending days explicitly selects calendar dates and removes the implicit observed-time bound. Pass `days` explicitly, or `date_start`/`date_end`, whenever the window matters.

near.description: Point proximity `lat,lon`, combined with `radius_km`. The box is used for index pruning and rows are refined by true great-circle distance.

limit.description: Maximum number of summary buckets. Each bucket returns counts plus metrics/metric_stats with avg/max/min generated metric aggregates. There is no continuation cursor; narrow the window when this cap is reached.

admin1.description: Optional state/province/admin1 name discovered with list_admin1. Filters Event location only. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'admin1').

domain.description: Deprecated legacy CAMEO+ domain filter. Prefer category/categories for new integrations.

entity.description: Restrict to an entity's resolved coverage. Accepts a spine id (`e_…`), a news id (`wiki:…`) or a name, resolved through the shared arbiter so the same handle means the same entity on every endpoint. Accepts up to 25 comma-separated handles, which are UNIONED: a row is returned if ANY handle matches, never only the rows matching all of them. Every handle resolves through that same arbiter, so a handle means the same entity alone or in a list. A handle that resolves to nothing contributes nothing — it never widens the result — and is named in `applied_filters.entity_handles_unresolved`. More than 25 handles is refused with 400 MULTIPLE_ENTITY_HANDLES rather than truncated. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'entity').

office.description: Restrict to the OFFICE-HOLDERS of a political office: the Wikidata QID of the office (`Q…`) or the `p_…` id `/api/v2/offices` serves. Resolves to every holder whose published term overlaps the window (or `office_as_of`, when sent), then scopes exactly as `entity=<those holders>` would — a row is returned if ANY holder matches, and it is UNIONED with `entity=` when both are sent. A name is refused with 400; resolve it with `GET /api/v2/offices?q=` first. A roster of more than 1,000 holders inside the window is refused with 400 OFFICE_SCOPE_TOO_LARGE, never truncated. Holders reach the news layer only through a Wikipedia identity, so `applied_filters.office_holders` discloses how many of the roster are `bridged_to_news` versus `unbridged` — an unbridged holder carries no key coverage matching can match on and contributes no rows, so the counts are a FLOOR on the office's real coverage rather than a measurement of it. Each matched row carries `entity_link.via: "office"` with `entity_link.entity` naming the HOLDER (a spine id), not the office. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'office').

region.description: One plain-English region (Middle East, Europe, South Asia, Western Africa, …). Expanded to its ISO-3 country list and applied the same way as `country`.

search.description: Case-insensitive literal phrase in Event title/summary or Story title.

country.description: One or more plain-English country names or ISO-3 codes; legacy FIPS aliases also accepted. Same OR'd location-or-actor-origin semantics as search_events. For a single country pass a one-element list: country=['United States']. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'country').

category.description: One category string, e.g. Battles or INFRASTRUCTURE. Use categories for multiple choices. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'category').

end_date.description: Inclusive end date in YYYY-MM-DD. With days only, start_date is computed as the trailing window ending here. Defaults to today UTC.

group_by.description: Dashboard grouping dimension. Use 'date' for trend lines, geography for maps, category for top taxonomy buckets, and subcategory to discover scoped drilldowns such as Battles -> Government regains territory. The two actor dimensions bucket by actor ORIGIN rather than by where the event happened — pair source_actor_country with a source filter to answer 'X acted on whom, ranked' in one call. Buckets include aggregate metrics used in significance scoring. NOTE: summarize_stories does NOT accept the actor dimensions — a Story has no source/target actor of its own.

continent.description: One plain-English continent (Asia, Europe, Africa, North America, South America, Oceania). Expanded to its ISO-3 country list and applied the same way as `country`.

languages.description: Coverage-language filter (ISO 639-1/2) on the underlying articles. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'languages').

radius_km.description: Distance in kilometres from the selected point for geographic proximity matching.

categories.description: JSON array (OR combined), e.g. ["INFRASTRUCTURE", "ECONOMIC"], not a JSON-encoded string. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'categories').

start_date.description: Inclusive start date in YYYY-MM-DD. With end_date, defines an explicit MCP summary window of at most 30 days.

target_ids.description: Comma-separated stable IDs for the selected roots (up to 25). Use with target_type; roots are unioned. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'target_ids').

subcategory.description: Event subcategory string validated at runtime, scoped by category/categories. For CAMEO+ categories, prefer stable event codes such as TE01 or IN03; codebook labels are accepted as legacy aliases. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'subcategory').

office_as_of.description: VALID TIME for `office=` — scope to whoever held the office ON this date (YYYY-MM-DD) rather than to everyone whose term overlaps the window. This is the publisher's start/end clock, not what we knew then: it is NOT the knowledge-time `as_of` and is not gated by it. Office-holders with no published start date cannot be placed on a date and are excluded (counted in `applied_filters.office_holders.undated_excluded`), never fabricated. Ignored without `office`.

actor_country.description: EITHER side, ignoring direction — the actor-origin half of `country` on its own. Use it to exclude events that merely HAPPENED in a country with no actor from it. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'actor_country').

Pass `country_match=location` when you need the two to agree.

fields.description: Restrict to the OFFICE-HOLDERS of a political office: the Wikidata QID of the office (`Q…`) or the `p_…` id `/api/v2/offices` serves. Resolves to every holder whose published term overlaps the window (or `office_as_of`, when sent), then scopes exactly as `entity=<those holders>` would — a row is returned if ANY holder matches, and it is UNIONED with `entity=` when both are sent. A name is refused with 400; resolve it with `GET /api/v2/offices?q=` first. A roster of more than 1,000 holders inside the window is refused with 400 OFFICE_SCOPE_TOO_LARGE, never truncated. Holders reach the news layer only through a Wikipedia identity, so `applied_filters.office_holders` discloses how many of the roster are `bridged_to_news` versus `unbridged` — an unbridged holder carries no key coverage matching can match on and contributes no rows, so the counts are a FLOOR on the office's real coverage rather than a measurement of it. Each matched row carries `entity_link.via: "office"` with `entity_link.entity` naming the HOLDER (a spine id), not the office. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_events', 'office').

tool.name: summarize_stories
tool.title: GDELT Cloud: summarize stories
tool.description: Compare reporting counts with identical structured filters; use summarize_events for Event metrics. These are coverage statistics, not operational losses. Continuous stories coverage begins 2026-03-08. Use consecutive windows of at most 30 inclusive days; a calendar month can be too long. This summary endpoint does not support cursor pagination; request each date chunk separately. Without an explicit window, entity filters default to 30 days and other queries to the last 24 hours. meta.query_window reports the effective predicates; meta.coverage describes the available corpus. Summarize v2 Stories for dashboards, coverage maps, and trend charts. Use before drilling into Stories when the user asks for story counts, article volume, linked-event coverage, or fatality coverage by date, geography, category, or subcategory. Category/subcategory rollups use linked Event taxonomy, so they are good for coverage counts by Conflict event type or sub-event type. Does not accept semantic search. Returns grouped aggregate metric statistics: article counts, linked Event metrics, fatalities and recency. Favor the four core metrics when analyzing linked Events: magnitude, systemic importance, propagation potential and market sensitivity; significance is a ranking aid. Hide coding confidence in ordinary answers. Use returned non-null measurement counts; Story averages are coverage statistics, not an incident-risk index. For country/region briefs read_resource skill://news-country-research/SKILL.md.

has_fatalities.description: Set true to summarize only Stories linked to fatal Events. Implies has_events=true.

event_categories.description: Deprecated alias for categories. Prefer categories=[...].

article_count_max.description: Maximum article count threshold for Story coverage.

article_count_min.description: Minimum article count threshold for Story coverage.

civilian_targeting.description: Set true to summarize only Stories linked to Conflict Events where ACLED civilian_targeting is populated.

country_attribution.description: For group_by=country: primary preserves one primary country per Story; all counts each Story under every authoritative country attribution or linked Event location/actor origin, using the same country_match and other filters as the Stories list. Explicit geographic filters also restrict the emitted country buckets. Buckets overlap and must not be summed as a global total. Other groupings ignore this option.

x-gdelt-taxonomy.subcategory_rule: Subcategory is validated against its parent category/categories. Use stable returned codes; legacy labels are accepted aliases. Unknown choices fail before billing. For unfamiliar labels, search get_event_taxonomy with a known category and the default page size.
x-gdelt-taxonomy.subcategory_discovery: Optional get_event_taxonomy(category=...) or get_parameter_options with parent_value scopes the choices; familiar valid filters need no lookup.

inputSchema.x-gdelt-errorRecovery: Use category/categories for linked Event taxonomy. If validation fails, choose from compact accepted_values when present, otherwise use nearest_values or run a subcategory summary.

items.description: One aggregate bucket. Counts: event_count, conflict_event_count, cameoplus_event_count, fatality_event_count, fatalities, article_count. Plus avg/min/max metric rollups and nested `metrics`/`metric_stats` (significance, goldstein, cameoplus, confidence, article_count, fatalities).

else.description: Aggregate rollup grouped by `group_by` (one entry per bucket).

data.description: Compact records retain IDs, returned links, selected images, evidence and metrics where available; unknown values remain unknown.

_mcp_projection.description: Explicitly discloses omitted fields or shortened evidence.

Pass `country_match=location` when you need the two to agree.

fields.description: Restrict to an entity's resolved coverage. Accepts a spine id (`e_…`), a news id (`wiki:…`) or a name, resolved through the shared arbiter so the same handle means the same entity on every endpoint. Accepts up to 25 comma-separated handles, which are UNIONED: a row is returned if ANY handle matches, never only the rows matching all of them. Every handle resolves through that same arbiter, so a handle means the same entity alone or in a list. A handle that resolves to nothing contributes nothing — it never widens the result — and is named in `applied_filters.entity_handles_unresolved`. More than 25 handles is refused with 400 MULTIPLE_ENTITY_HANDLES rather than truncated. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_stories', 'entity').

fields.description: Which canonical ids the handle stands for. `expand` (default) also matches the sibling ids the entity arbiter has already merged into the same real-world entity — a Wikipedia identity minted twice under different URL spellings, for instance — and echoes the union back as `applied_filters.entity_ids_expanded`. `exact` restricts to the one canonical id the handle resolves to, reproducing the pre-2026-08-25 counts.

fields.description: Restrict to the OFFICE-HOLDERS of a political office: the Wikidata QID of the office (`Q…`) or the `p_…` id `/api/v2/offices` serves. Resolves to every holder whose published term overlaps the window (or `office_as_of`, when sent), then scopes exactly as `entity=<those holders>` would — a row is returned if ANY holder matches, and it is UNIONED with `entity=` when both are sent. A name is refused with 400; resolve it with `GET /api/v2/offices?q=` first. A roster of more than 1,000 holders inside the window is refused with 400 OFFICE_SCOPE_TOO_LARGE, never truncated. Holders reach the news layer only through a Wikipedia identity, so `applied_filters.office_holders` discloses how many of the roster are `bridged_to_news` versus `unbridged` — an unbridged holder carries no key coverage matching can match on and contributes no rows, so the counts are a FLOOR on the office's real coverage rather than a measurement of it. Each matched row carries `entity_link.via: "office"` with `entity_link.entity` naming the HOLDER (a spine id), not the office. Choices: get_parameter_options('summarize_stories', 'office').

fields.description: VALID TIME for `office=` — scope to whoever held the office ON this date (YYYY-MM-DD) rather than to everyone whose term overlaps the window. Office-holders with no published start date cannot be placed on a date and are excluded (counted in `applied_filters.office_holders.undated_excluded`), never fabricated. Ignored without `office`.

tool.name: unified_entity_search
tool.title: Resolve an entity identity
tool.description: Resolve a name, alias or acronym to cross-source identity candidates from public reporting, corporate/LEI, energy, restricted-party, finance and AI-compute reference data. Use for 'which entity is this?' before an ID-backed query or Monitor; search_entities instead measures actors appearing in a reporting window. Returns candidates, canonical entity_id where resolved, matching evidence, identifiers and sources availability. Unavailable source keys are DELETED from sources when WITHHELD by entitlement, not set false. An absent key means not searched; only a present false means checked with no match. Do not infer restricted-party status, source absence or news coverage from withheld results. country_match=strict checks source country association; include_unknown explicitly broadens it. Association is distinct from nationality, headquarters and reporting geography. Clarify consequential ambiguity. type=facility returns facility_id, distinct from the owner. holds_office selects a published role; holders remain persons. With universe=osint and holds_office=true, omit q to browse officials using sort=name and pagination.next_offset. osint returns publisher reference records that may have no entity_id; inspect resolved_in_spine and meta.lanes. universe=registry is the legal-entity LEI lane and does not accept holds_office. Source identity evidence is not a compliance determination or inference of private personal traits.

q.description: Canonical search text: a name, alias, or acronym. Required except when browsing public officials with universe=osint and holds_office=true. Until native non-Latin-script matching ships, use a common Romanized or English spelling for Cyrillic, Chinese, and other non-Latin names.

sort.description: Use name for stable alphabetical public-official browsing with universe=osint and holds_office=true. Default when q is absent.

type.description: Optional identity type used to narrow ambiguous candidates. Conflicting linked types retain entity_type=entity and type_evidence; a filtered result includes a conflict only when the requested type is a published possibility. facility searches the existing facility directory and returns facility_id, not an invented entity ID. Source entitlements apply.

limit.description: Number of records to return on this page; pagination describes how to continue.

offset.description: Number of records to skip before this page.

region.description: Geographic region whose member countries define the scope.

country.description: Known country association from source records, not an assertion of headquarters, citizenship, or reporting location. Accepts country names, ISO-2 or ISO-3; comma-separate for OR. Use country_match=strict for candidates with known matching evidence. Choices: get_parameter_options('unified_entity_search', 'country').

universe.description: Search all merged entities, news entities, reference entities, raw GLEIF registry records, or OSINT list and office-holder records. The registry and osint lanes return source records with nullable entity_id; they do not establish news coverage. Source entitlements apply.

continent.description: Continent whose member countries define the geographic scope.

holds_office.description: Only politicians: entities that hold or have held a published public office (`sources.offices`), or on `universe=osint` only office-holder records. A ROLE filter, not a type — an office-holder is a `person`. Requires `can_use_offices` (403 PLAN_REQUIRED otherwise) and is not applicable to `universe=registry` (legal entities only; 400).

country_match.description: strict requires known matching source country association; include_unknown also returns candidates with no country evidence. Recommended requests explicitly send strict. Omission retains include_unknown compatibility.

response_mode.description: Compact chat projection or unchanged bounded full API response; neither fetches another page.

include_images.description: Retain source article image URLs on returned cards when available.

score.description: Resolver match strength, not a probability or a coverage count.

sources.description: Facilities may list source identifiers. Entity maps preserve null for unknown coverage. Per-source availability booleans: news, sec, gem, sanctions, china, wiki, epoch, gov. ★ A GATED SOURCE THE CALLER'S PLAN DOES NOT INCLUDE IS DELETED FROM THIS MAP, NOT SET FALSE (sec, sanctions, china, epoch_ai, gov). An ABSENT key means WITHHELD — we did not look on this caller's behalf; only a key PRESENT and `false` means 'we looked and found none'. Reporting a missing key as no coverage is the measured defect this wording exists to prevent: a Professional caller was told RTX Corporation had no federal awards while it held 111 worth $44.3B.

spine_id.description: Canonical e_ entity ID when resolved; null when no canonical ID is available.

entity_id.description: Stable entity id (e_, wiki: or llm:) when available. Facility and unlinked source records have null; never use osint_ref or LEI as an entity Monitor id.

match_type.description: Lexical evidence such as exact_name, exact_alias, token_set or fuzzy_name.

entity_type.description: Canonical type, or neutral entity when linked source records conflict. Read type_evidence before treating that candidate as a person or organization.

facility_id.description: Canonical facility identity when type=facility, separate from its owner entity and nearby Events.

identifiers.description: Cross-source id map keyed by id_type (us_sec_cik, ticker, gem, epoch_org, aiddata_financier, ...) → list of values. Redacted the same way as `sources`: the id types behind a gated source the caller is not entitled to are DELETED, so a missing id_type means withheld, not absent.

country_iso3.description: Candidate ISO-3 countries used for disambiguation when known.

coverage_30d.description: Measured recent Story coverage. Zero is measured absence; null or omitted coverage is unknown, never zero.

entity_id.description: Supporting source record identity; it may be a merged-away reference ID.

entity_type.description: Unmodified type asserted by this source record.

type_evidence.description: Optional unresolved type evidence. Type filters may retain the candidate only when the requested family is a published possibility; they do not resolve the disagreement or replace the stable identity.

country_evidence.description: Basis and explanation of source country association; no known evidence has a null basis.

source_universes.description: Which universes matched: media, geg_wiki, reference.

items.description: One real-world entity deduped across sources. `sources` is the per-source availability map and `identifiers` the cross-source join keys — the value a builder uses to bridge this entity across news / SEC filings / GEM energy / sanctions / China / Epoch AI. A gated source the caller is not entitled to is DELETED from both maps, so an absent key means WITHHELD, never absent.

pagination.description: Present for alphabetical public-official browsing. Continue with next_offset; null means exhausted.

applied_filters.description: Echo of canonical query, universe, role and type filters.

else.description: Cross-source entity candidates deduped to one real-world entity per hit. `data` is the candidate list; default-universe `sources`/`identifiers` carry the cross-source join keys. Explicit osint/registry universes return publisher reference records, possibly without entity_id. Both maps are redacted per plan by DELETING gated keys, so absent means withheld, not absent.

data.description: Compact records retain IDs, returned links, selected images, evidence and metrics where available; unknown values remain unknown.

pagination.description: Present for alphabetical public-official browsing. Continue with next_offset; null means exhausted.

tool.name: gdelt_cloud_monitor_form
tool.title: Review Monitor draft
tool.description: When the user asks to prepare, edit or review a Monitor, call this read-only tool to open its interactive form; do not substitute a code-block template. Country/category and email/webhook controls are provided. Use countries, cameoplus_domains/conflict_categories and daily_hour from the schema; omit enabled (Preview is always unsaved). Pass validated direct preview_monitor parameters; never saves or sends. Returns monitor_form with draft, scope and preview receipt. Preview consumes metered usage when admitted; its receipt is an unsaved test, never a completed scheduled checkpoint. Do not claim rendering without client evidence. Wait for confirmation before creation; use validated text only if rendering is unavailable.

data.description: Whether legacy subjects match Events, Stories or both. Omission preserves events_and_stories; omit for query subjects, whose endpoint determines the data.

name.description: Short name for the Monitor being previewed.

email.description: Retained email-delivery setting for the draft. Preview never sends email and needs no delivery channel.

region.description: Geographic region for a geography subject, or a geographic refinement of another Monitor subject.

search.description: Semantic Event/Story content to match. Required for topic Monitors. This is not entity-name resolution; use unified_entity_search first.

cadence.description: How often the Monitor checks for newly matching records, subject to the connected account entitlement.

latitude.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, north-positive, for the place Monitor center; used with longitude.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name used to interpret the daily schedule, such as America/New_York. Choices: get_parameter_options('preview_monitor', 'timezone').

continent.description: Continent for a geography subject, or a geographic refinement of another Monitor subject.

countries.description: ISO-3 countries for a geography Monitor, or geographic refinements of another subject. Choices: get_parameter_options('preview_monitor', 'countries').

longitude.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, east-positive, for the place Monitor center; used with latitude.

radius_km.description: Distance in kilometres around a facility or point target. Omission preserves the REST radius of 25 km; omit for query subjects.

daily_hour.description: Hour of the daily check in the selected timezone; retained but ignored for hourly cadence.

entity_ids.description: Resolved entity IDs from unified_entity_search. Select the intended candidates and reuse their e_, wiki: or llm: IDs; never pass bare names. Choices: get_parameter_options('preview_monitor', 'entity_ids').

monitor_id.description: Organization Monitor UUID returned by create_monitor or list_monitors; select a Monitor in the connected organization. Choices: get_parameter_options('preview_monitor', 'monitor_id').

target_ids.description: Resolved selected entity/facility IDs. Selected-item limit is account-dependent; clarify consequential identity ambiguity. Choices: get_parameter_options('preview_monitor', 'target_ids').

description.description: Human-readable purpose or instructions associated with the Monitor draft.

facility_id.description: Canonical facility identifier returned by facilities_search or unified_entity_search; reuse the selected facility ID. Choices: get_parameter_options('preview_monitor', 'facility_id').

search_mode.description: Content matching mode; omission preserves the API default.

target_type.description: For connected Monitors: entity or facility. Prefer this subject for company or asset watches.

webhook_url.description: Draft webhook destination. Preview retains it but never contacts it and does not require it.

history_days.description: Setup history: 7 days by default, or 30. Preview never establishes a scheduled checkpoint or sends delivery; incomplete history remains explicit.

query_params.description: Saved filters for query_endpoint. Resolve names first and reuse selected IDs. Omit fixed dates and pagination because scheduled execution supplies its own window and page bounds. Choices: get_parameter_options('preview_monitor', 'query_params').

source_updates.description: Connected source update groups. Discover exact choices through get_parameter_options. Omit for source defaults; [] disables source updates.

fatalities_only.description: Restrict compatible conflict Events to records with fatalities.

nearby_radius_km.description: Explicit opt-in nearby Events for connected facilities. Omission does not add proximity; never infer an outage from nearby news.

story_categories.description: Story-level topics to watch; distinct from the linked Events taxonomy.

conflict_categories.description: Conflict Event types to watch, such as Battles; scope by what happened rather than Story topic.

scope.description: Readable subject and filter interpretation for review.

status.description: Preparation status.

preview_receipt.description: Observed match/coverage receipt from the metered Preview; a Preview is not a saved Monitor or scheduled checkpoint.

monitor_form.description: Validated unsaved draft, readable scope and match receipt. Webhook URL is omitted; the user may enter it privately in the form.

tool.name: energy_search_assets
tool.title: Search energy assets
tool.description: Search native Global Energy Monitor records for technology and ownership detail. For country-context asset lists or nearby infrastructure, prefer facilities_search with source=[gem], which returns public GDELT Cloud facility links. This specialist spans v2 trackers: coal plants, coal mines, coal terminals, oil & gas plants, oil & gas extraction fields, LNG terminals, nuclear, geothermal, bioenergy, hydropower, solar, and wind. Geography filters (country, region, continent) use the same ISO-3 expansion as search_events, so cross-product analyses ('events near energy assets in region X') stay consistent. Filter by status (operating/proposed/retired/etc.), fuel, capacity range (MW for power generation), start year, owner substring or GEM Entity ID, geographic bbox or radius proximity ('near'), and asset name. Returns clean asset cards with capacity, location, ownership chain (owners/operators/parents with stake percentages), GEM Wiki URL, and a detail_url for drilldown via energy_get_asset. GEM links credit the source; they do not replace facility-page citations.

bbox.description: Geographic viewport: 'lat_min,lon_min,lat_max,lon_max'. Returns assets with lat/lon inside the bounding box.

fuel.description: Normalized fuel class of the selected asset. Use the values in this schema; native source fuel labels are returned evidence, not accepted filter values.

near.description: Proximity query: 'lat,lon,radius_km'. Returns assets within the radius. Use for 'energy assets near event location'.

sort.description: 'capacity_desc' for largest first; 'capacity_mw' is accepted as a backward-compatible alias for 'capacity_desc'; 'start_year_desc' for newest; 'recent' for most-recently-updated; 'name' for alphabetical.

tier.description: Tier discriminator within a tracker. 'main' (default for most), 'sub_threshold' (oil_gas_plants), 'below_threshold' (wind, hydropower), 'utility' (solar 1MW+), 'distributed' (solar <1MW), 'closed' (coal_mines closed sheet). tool.name: energy_summarize_assets
tool.title: Summarize energy assets
tool.description: First call for capacity rollups, energy mix breakdowns, transition tracking, ownership-share totals, and 'biggest / largest / top by capacity' questions across the Global Energy Monitor registry. For representative sites, pair this rollup with facilities_search (source=[gem]) and its public facility URLs; energy_search_assets is for deeper native detail. Group by country, region, continent, tracker, status, start_year_decade, fuel, or tier. Returns count + sum/avg/min/max capacity_mw + a status breakdown per bucket. CRITICAL: capacity_mw is only meaningful for power generation trackers (coal_plants, oil_gas_plants, nuclear, geothermal, bioenergy, hydropower, solar, wind); for coal_mines (Mtpa), coal_terminals (Mt), lng_terminals (Mtpa or Bcm/y), and oil_gas_extraction (no capacity), capacity_mw will be 0 — constrain with the tracker filter when summing capacity. Use for status-filtered native units and capacity by country/owner. Asset counts are not station counts; nameplate MW is not generation or uptime. Keep source vintage explicit.

tool.name: screening_match
tool.title: Screen an entity
tool.description: Compare a supplied name or organizational identifier against published restricted-party lists. Returns candidate identity evidence, publisher list/programme references, dates and optional reported ownership-chain exposure. Supports organizations, public-source person records, vessels and aircraft. Similarity or a shared name is not proof of identity; inspect corroborating source evidence. A no-match result is not clearance, and list categories differ. Use for researching a counterparty's published list evidence; no legal/compliance determination or enforcement action is made. Do not supply private personal government identifiers.

q.description: Counterparty name to screen against restricted-party lists.

id.description: Strong id (LEI / registration number) for an exact, deterministic match. Choices: get_parameter_options('screening_match', 'id').

as_of.description: Historical observation date in YYYY-MM-DD. Omission screens currently active memberships; historical gaps remain inconclusive rather than a clean result.

limit.description: Maximum number of matches.

birth_year.description: PERSON EVIDENCE, not a filter. Year of birth of the subject, compared with a ±1 tolerance because lists publish approximate and circa dates. A candidate whose recorded year contradicts it beyond that tolerance moves to rejected_candidates with decision_evidence: birth_year_mismatch; agreement is reported as evidence.birth_year: match; a candidate with no recorded year is unknown and stays a candidate. There is deliberately no date-of-birth parameter — the served person field is a YEAR.

nationality.description: PERSON EVIDENCE, not a filter. Nationality / citizenship of the subject as ISO-3 codes (e.g. ['IRN','IRQ']). Compared against each candidate's country_iso3 and reported per candidate as evidence.nationality (match | mismatch | unknown). It never narrows retrieval and never rejects on its own, because list country fields are inconsistently populated. An unresolvable code returns 400 INVALID_COUNTRY.

response_mode.description: Compact chat projection or unchanged bounded full API response; neither fetches another page.

include_exposure.description: Attach ownership-chain exposure context to accepted matches.

min_match_confidence.description: Threshold for calibrated identity confidence. Retrieval similarity is returned separately and is not a probability.

birth_year.description: The birth year sent as person evidence; null when none was sent.

nationality.description: The ISO-3 nationalities sent as person evidence, resolved; null when none was sent.

birth_year.description: Birth YEAR the list publishes for a natural-person row (entity_kind = individual); null when the row is not a person or the list did not publish one. A year, never a date, by the served-person contract (schema 171).

match_score.description: Candidate-retrieval similarity for this list row; not an identity probability.

score.description: Deprecated compatibility copy of retrieval_score; not an identity probability.

birth_year.description: `match` = a contributing list row records a year within ±1 of the query; `mismatch` = every row that records a year contradicts it beyond ±1 (the candidate is then in rejected_candidates); `unknown` = no contributing row records a year.

nationality.description: `match` = a contributing row's country_iso3 is one of the query nationalities; `mismatch` = every row that records a country disagrees; `unknown` = no row records one. Reported, never used to reject — list country fields are inconsistently populated.

evidence.description: Per-candidate verdicts for the person evidence the caller sent (`birth_year`, `nationality`). Absent when neither was sent.

confidence.description: Compatibility retrieval band. Do not use it as an identity verdict; use decision and match_confidence.

retrieval_score.description: Retrieval ranking score only; it is not calibrated identity confidence.

script_handling.description: How cross-script identity evidence was handled. unknown means no supported determination was made.

match_confidence.description: Calibrated identity confidence. Currently 1 for deterministic verified identifiers/exact names and null for uncalibrated gray candidates.

retrieval_method.description: How the candidate was retrieved. Fuzzy and semantic retrieval expand recall and are independently adjudicated.

screen_status.description: matches = conclusive hit. inconclusive = unresolved candidate evidence, OR no screen was possible (see inconclusive_reason). out_of_scope = the subject is a natural person and the corpus is institution-only, so nothing was screened. no_match_found = screened against the covered lists and nothing was found — which is still not compliance clearance.

per_source.description: One row per ingested list: whether it has MEASURED person rows, and how many.

individual_sources.description: The source_keys a natural person is actually screened against. Empty = persons are out of scope.

subject_scope.description: Which subject types the restricted-party corpus can speak about, per source. Machine-readable because the caller has to branch on it: a person is screened only against `individual_sources`, and a `no_match_found` for a person says nothing about the institution-only lists.

coverage_window.description: The dates this endpoint can be screened AGAINST. These are our observation dates, not designation dates — an `as_of` before `start` is refused as inconclusive rather than answered.

inconclusive_reason.description: Why no determination was reached. Present on screen_status=inconclusive when the cause is structural rather than evidential.

birth_year.description: `match` = a contributing list row records a year within ±1 of the query; `mismatch` = every row that records a year contradicts it beyond ±1 (the candidate is then in rejected_candidates); `unknown` = no contributing row records a year.

nationality.description: `match` = a contributing row's country_iso3 is one of the query nationalities; `mismatch` = every row that records a country disagrees; `unknown` = no row records one. Reported, never used to reject — list country fields are inconsistently populated.

decision_evidence.description: Why the candidate was rejected. `birth_year_mismatch` is the machine-readable value when the query `birth_year` contradicted every recorded year beyond ±1; otherwise the independent judge's rationale.

subject_type_detected.description: What our entity registry says the subject IS, by exact normalized name — present when the registry types it unambiguously. `person` with an empty `subject_scope.individual_sources` is why a screen is `out_of_scope`; `person` with person-bearing sources means the screen ran against exactly those. Absent when the registry does not know the name or types it both ways.

tool.name: maritime_activity
tool.title: Read vessel activity
tool.description: Aggregate vessel activity over a chokepoint / bbox / proximity area, bucketed by hour or day (≤30-day window) — distinct vessels, positions, moving positions, and avg/max speed per bucket. The 'is this area's traffic anomalous vs the baseline' view; generalizes maritime_transits to arbitrary geography. Reads raw positions; admin-only. Returns bucket, data time buckets with vessels, positions, moving_positions and avg_sog/max_sog in knots, plus pagination and applied_filters. Position counts are observations, not vessel counts.

days.description: Trailing N-day window.

near.description: Return activity within radius_km of a point, formatted 'lat,lon'. Default radius 50 km.

limit.description: Maximum number of buckets.

bucket.description: Time bucket: 'hour' or 'day'. Auto-picks hour for ≤2-day spans, else day.

date_end.description: Window end YYYY-MM-DD.

radius_km.description: Radius in km for near / near_gem_id (defaults: 50 for near, 25 for near_gem_id).

date_start.description: Window start YYYY-MM-DD (≤30-day window).

tool.name: maritime_port_pulse
tool.title: Read port disruption signals
tool.description: Port-level disruption intelligence — fuses the ports reference with GDELT Cloud Events near each port (event volume, conflict signal, a 7d-vs-baseline anomaly ratio, recent headlines) plus nearby energy-asset exposure and AIS-coverage context. The supply-chain / commodity product: 'which ports are making news, with what, and do we have maritime visibility there.' Scope by country, terminal type, or proximity. Returns port records with nearby reported Events, anomaly comparisons, energy exposure and AIS coverage context. Retain the signal windows and coverage; proximity is not established site impact.

bbox.description: Bounding box 'minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat' (lon-first) to scope the ports.

days.description: GDELT Cloud Event window in days (default 14).

near.description: Scope to ports within radius_km of a point, formatted 'lat,lon'. Default radius 200 km.

limit.description: Maximum number of ports.

region.description: One plain-English region (Middle East, Europe, Eastern Europe, South Asia, Western Africa, …). Expanded to its ISO-3 country list and applied the same way as `country` to scope the ports in view.

search.description: Port name / UN/LOCODE (substring) to scope to specific ports (e.g. 'Odesa').

country.description: Country filter — accepts a country name or ISO-2/ISO-3 code (e.g. UKR, EGY, Ukraine, UA) to scope the ports in view. Choices: get_parameter_options('maritime_port_pulse', 'country').

unlocode.description: United Nations port location code returned by maritime_ports; selects that port. Choices: get_parameter_options('maritime_port_pulse', 'unlocode').

continent.description: One plain-English continent (Asia, Europe, Africa, North America, South America, Oceania). Expanded to its ISO-3 country list and applied the same way as `country`.

radius_km.description: Radius in km for near / near_gem_id (default 200).

near_gem_id.description: GEM asset identifier from energy_search_assets, used as the center for nearby vessel or port observations. Choices: get_parameter_options('maritime_port_pulse', 'near_gem_id').

lng_terminal.description: true → only ports with an LNG terminal.

oil_terminal.description: true → only ports with an oil terminal.

response_mode.description: Compact chat projection or unchanged bounded full API response; neither fetches another page.

event_radius_km.description: How close (km) an event must be to a port to count for it (default 50).

min_harbor_size.description: Minimum harbor size: very_small | small | medium | large.

pulse_level.description: `critical` = at least 5 conflict Events; `elevated` = 1–4 conflict Events; `active` = no conflict Events but at least one other relevant Event; `quiet` = no relevant Events. Relevant-event volume does not override a conflict-based level.

ais_coverage.description: `live`, `sparse`, or `dark` is the observed AIS presence at the nearest sampled chokepoint coverage box within 160 km. `no_coverage` means the port is outside every sampled box and its catchment; it is not a claim that no vessels exist at the port.

anomaly_ratio.description: Last-7d event volume vs the windowed weekly baseline; null when there is no baseline.

relevant_events.description: Events within event_radius_km that are either conflict-family Events or carry one of the published maritime, infrastructure, trade, sanctions, energy, logistics, port, shipping, pipeline, customs, smuggling, or commodity relevance tags.

tool.name: facilities_context
tool.title: Read facility reporting context
tool.description: Facility plus bounded owner/parent news context. coverage_paths names each typed relationship, stake and source; minority ownership does not establish control. News is about the named entities, not necessarily located at or affecting the facility. NULL means unavailable; summaries count the returned preview. Name-only owners have separate reported_owner_matches and reported_owner_events/stories from unique exact reference-name or alias discovery. This does not verify ownership or alter resolved owner_events; inspect meta.reported_owner_coverage for measured/partial name scope. Optional include=nearby adds a separately labeled geographic screen with coordinate precision and reporting date coverage; proximity is not a confirmed site incident. Optional gov degrades when unentitled or the scope has multiple entities. Existing can_use_facilities gate and shared REST quotas apply. Use to join a canonical physical site, source participants and nearby reporting; proximity does not prove operational impact.

include.description: Optional extra blocks. `gov` attaches the owner's federal-award / FARA / sanctions footprint. An unentitled plan degrades the block to null with a `sources_unavailable` entry — it never 403s the whole response. `nearby` attaches Events within radius_km and their linked Stories. Nearby reporting is a geographic lead, not a confirmed incident at the site. Choices: get_parameter_options('facilities_context', 'include').

tool.name: facilities_search
tool.title: Search facilities
tool.description: Search the unified facilities directory — GEM energy assets (plants, mines, terminals, pipelines), mineral and industrial facilities, data centers, and ports. Reviewed fusion retains source memberships and unit observations. Filter by name, leaf type (coal_plant, lng_terminal, port, data_center, …) or coarse class (power/extraction/transport_logistics/digital_infrastructure), source silo, country/region/continent, commodity, owner, source-reported participant entity and exact participant role, status, capacity (MW), and geography (bbox/near). Participant roles are open-vocabulary source assertions, separate from ownership; matching cards retain bounded evidence and disclose truncation. sort=news_activity ranks by direct-owner Events first, then the distinct owner/nearby Event union over seven recent served days and 25 km. Read card.news_activity and meta.news_activity; owner and nearby counts overlap, and nearby reporting does not establish site impact. Multi-unit capacity_mw is not a site total; first/last_seen are observation dates, not source vintage or live uptime. Use returned url for public facility links; dataset credits are attribution. START HERE for 'which facilities are near / owned by / of type X'.

q.description: Facility name. Default lexical mode keeps case-insensitive substring matching. Opt-in search_mode=fuzzy suggests names with matching prefixes or small spelling errors; every query token must match a name token. These are selectable candidates, not resolved site identity. No embedding or inference runs.

bbox.description: Geographic viewport 'lat_min,lon_min,lat_max,lon_max'. Returns facilities with coordinates inside the box (geo-null facilities excluded).

near.description: Proximity query 'lat,lon,radius_km'. Returns facilities within the radius of a point — use for 'facilities near this event location'.

sort.description: 'name' | 'capacity_desc' (largest MW first) | 'capacity_asc' | 'recent' (directory updates) | 'country' | 'relevance' (requires q; literal names before fuzzy candidates) | 'news_activity' (seven recent served days: direct-owner Events first, then distinct owner/nearby Events within 25 km; see returned counts and meta.news_activity). Nearby reporting is not a site incident.

type.description: One or more leaf facility types from this schema, including mineral_mine, mineral_processing_plant, manufacturing_factory and data_center. Omit for all types. Choices: get_parameter_options('facilities_search', 'type').

tool.name: entity_tone
tool.title: Media Intelligence: entity tone
tool.description: Media tone toward a RESOLVED entity over time — mean tone on a -100..100 scale (negative = critical/adversarial coverage, positive = favorable), with the article/source coverage behind it. The headline `tone_score` BLENDS news coverage with (on some entity-days) recent Bluesky posts; the PRESS-only reading is `news_tone_score` and the social-only one is `social_tone_score`, reported side by side on rows[], entity_coverage[], evidence_samples[] and language_breakdown[]. Quote news_tone_score, not the headline, for a claim about press coverage. NOT public opinion, sentiment polling, or approval, and distinct from risk. Missing evidence is unavailable, not neutral — empty buckets mean no measured coverage, never a 0 reading, and a NULL component means NOT MEASURED (that source contributed no evidence, or the score predates the 2026-08-22 split and cannot be backfilled); 0 is the middle of the band. Read each component against its own denominator — `scored_news_story_count` / `scored_social_story_count` (and `news_article_count` / `social_article_count` per language, `news_evidence_count` / `social_evidence_count` per sample). Social is attached only to entities already in the news stream and never scored alone, so it backs a small minority of scored stories: a social tone quoted without its story count is a misreport. Pass `languages` (e.g. ['ar','zh','en']) to compare how the same entity is covered across language spheres. Start from a name with `entity` (it resolves) or a known `entity_id`.

days.description: Trailing window size in days, used only to complete the range when start_date or end_date is omitted.

entity.description: Entity to measure tone for, by name (e.g. 'Nvidia') or Wikipedia-keyed id. Resolved to a canonical entity before measuring; pass the name here when you don't already have an id. Either entity or entity_id is required. Choices: get_parameter_options('entity_tone', 'entity').

end_date.description: Inclusive end date in YYYY-MM-DD for the tone window. With days only, start_date is the trailing window ending here. Defaults to today UTC.

entity_id.description: Known v2/canonical Entity id (from unified_entity_search or get_entity). Use instead of entity when you already have the resolved id. Either entity or entity_id is required. Choices: get_parameter_options('entity_tone', 'entity_id').

languages.description: ISO source-language filter, e.g. ['ar','zh','en']. Restricts the tone timeline + coverage to articles in those source languages so you can compare how an entity is covered across language spheres. Omit for all languages. Choices: get_parameter_options('entity_tone', 'languages').

start_date.description: Inclusive start date in YYYY-MM-DD for the tone window. With end_date, defines a window of at most 30 days. Sent as start_date (this route reads start_date/start, not date_start).

response_mode.description: Compact chat projection or unchanged bounded full API response; neither fetches another page.

include_evidence.description: When true, attach a sample of the underlying scored articles (the evidence behind each tone reading) so the number is auditable rather than a bare score.

coverage_ratio.description: Share of candidate stories that produced a scored tone row, from 0 to 1. Read this before presenting the aggregate as representative.

agreement_score.description: Evidence agreement from 0 to 1: higher values mean the independent evidence items frame the entity more consistently; lower values mean mixed or conflicting framing.

avg_news_tone_score.description: Story-weighted mean tone over the NEWS evidence only, for this entity-day. null when no scored story that day carries a news reading — either the evidence was all social, or the day was scored before the split shipped (2026-08-22). Never read null as neutral: 0 is the middle of the band.

avg_social_tone_score.description: Story-weighted mean tone over the BLUESKY SOCIAL evidence only, for this entity-day. Not capped by avg_tone_score — where the two diverge sharply, that gap is the finding. null when not measured.

scored_news_story_count.description: Scored stories that day carrying a news reading. This is the DENOMINATOR of avg_news_tone_score; it is not scored_story_count.

scored_social_story_count.description: Scored stories that day carrying a social reading. Normally a small fraction of scored_story_count — social is attached only to entities already in the news stream. Read avg_social_tone_score against this, not against the headline.

mean_news_tone.description: The entity’s news-only tone over the whole window, weighted by scored_news_story_count. null when not measured.

mean_social_tone.description: The entity’s social-only tone over the whole window, weighted by scored_social_story_count. null when not measured.

scored_news_story_count.description: Scored stories in the window carrying a news reading — the denominator of mean_news_tone.

scored_social_story_count.description: Scored stories in the window carrying a social reading — the denominator of mean_social_tone.

tone_label.description: Human-readable band for tone_score. Null whenever tone_score is unavailable.

tone_score.description: Blended media-framing score from -100 (most negative) to 100 (most positive). Null means the story was not scored; 0 is a measured neutral reading.

evidence_uids.description: Index-aligned with evidence_snippets. A "bluesky:" prefix marks a social item.

conflict_label.description: Qualitative evidence-agreement band. `aligned` means consistent framing; `mixed` means material variation; `conflicting` means opposing readings; `insufficient` means there was not enough independent evidence to assess agreement.

agreement_score.description: Evidence agreement from 0 to 1: higher values mean the independent evidence items frame the entity more consistently; lower values mean mixed or conflicting framing.

canonical_title.description: English-preferred headline for the story; falls back to the representative title.

news_tone_score.description: Tone over this story’s NEWS evidence only. null when the story carried no news evidence for this entity (news_evidence_count = 0) or was scored before 2026-08-22.

evidence_snippets.description: Up to 4 quoted snippets the model read.

social_tone_score.description: Tone over this story’s BLUESKY SOCIAL evidence only. null when the story carried no social evidence (social_evidence_count = 0) or was scored before 2026-08-22.

news_evidence_count.description: Evidence items behind news_tone_score. Together with social_evidence_count this tells a null "no evidence of this kind" apart from a null "scored before the split".

evidence_source_urls.description: Index-aligned permalinks. EMPTY means not recorded (scored before 2026-08 attribution), never "no source".

evidence_samples.description: One card per scored story, returned when include_evidence=true. Capped by evidence_limit.

scored_rows.description: Scored (entity, story) rows contributing to this language.

article_count.description: All evidence items in this language.

avg_tone_score.description: Blended tone for stories covered in this language, weighted by that language’s evidence-item count.

news_article_count.description: Evidence items in this language behind avg_news_tone_score.

avg_news_tone_score.description: News-only tone for this language, weighted by news_article_count. null when no news evidence in this language carries a reading.

social_article_count.description: Evidence items in this language behind avg_social_tone_score.

avg_social_tone_score.description: Social-only tone for this language, weighted by social_article_count. null when none — never 0.

language_breakdown.description: Tone per evidence language over the FULL scored window (not the evidence sample), split by evidence source.

tool.name: offices_search
tool.title: Search public offices
tool.description: Published office evidence with incomplete source/country coverage; preserve undated and unresolved records. Search public political offices — legislative seats, cabinet posts, heads of state and government, courts, security/financial offices, IGO posts — one row per office with holder counts (holders_current is NULL, never 0, when no source asserts currency). Filter by country (ISO-3 / name, OR'd), scope (national | subnational | international), branch (legislative | executive | head | judicial | security | financial | igo | other), organization, has_holders, and as_of. q= is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING over the office name, not semantic search. START HERE to resolve an office name to its id (a Wikidata QID or p_… id) before passing office= to search_events / search_stories, or calling office_get / office_holders. Office-holders are ACTOR CONTEXT for events — NOT a PEP or sanctions-screening tool and never a compliance determination.

q.description: Case-insensitive SUBSTRING match over the office name (e.g. 'Minister of Finance', 'Member of Parliament'). Not semantic: a related term that does not appear literally will not match. Results keep the sort order, not relevance — narrow with country.

sort.description: name (default, A-Z) | holders_desc (most office-holders on record first) | country. The cursor is bound to the sort it was minted under — changing sort mid-walk is 400 CURSOR_STALE.

as_of.description: VALID TIME (YYYY-MM-DD): restrict to offices with at least one holder IN OFFICE on that date, read from the publisher's start/end dates, and attach holders_as_of to every row. Not knowledge-time replay. Office_holders with no published start date cannot be placed on a date and are EXCLUDED (meta.undated_office_holders counts them), never guessed. A future date reads as 'still in office as far as the source has published'.

tool.name: entity_hierarchy
tool.title: Legal Entities (GLEIF): entity hierarchy
tool.description: An entity's corporate hierarchy — direct parent, ultimate parent, children — resolved through the entity spine. Accepts a NAME, a resolved e_ id, a wiki: id, a wikipedia_url or a bare LEI, so it composes directly off search results without translating ids. ALWAYS read the `coverage` block first: lei_present=false means WE hold no LEI (a coverage gap, not 'no parent'), while a reporting_exception means the filer DECLARED an exception instead of naming one. Not ownership. Gated on can_use_exposure.

_published_faq.name: How do I add GDELT Cloud to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add GDELT Cloud to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.gdeltcloud.com/mcp.
